title: Progressive Egress Rehoming Protocol (draft)
body:
Summary:
This draft defines an operator-facing protocol for progressive egress rehoming: a controlled, staged shift of customer traffic away from a degraded region to healthy regions while minimizing cache evaporation, token cost spikes, and DNS/peering churn. The goal is to keep latency SLOs intact for most traffic while preserving warm caches and minimizing downstream load spikes.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goal: Rapid, reversible traffic rehoming with minimal customer-visible errors and bounded latency increases.
- Goal: Preserve KV/prefix caches to avoid token cost and cold-start CPU/GPU spikes.
- Non-goal: Full automated reroute for every failure mode. This is an operator-assisted procedure intended for partial-region degradations and capacity-driven evacuations.

Scope and when to use this protocol:
Use when a region shows sustained backend saturation, service degradation (p95 latency > 2x baseline for > 5m), or network egress anomalies limited to that region, AND where full DNS failover is undesirable because of cache loss or downstream capacity constraints. Not intended for complete region blackout (use full evacuation playbook).

Definitions and abbreviations:
- Origin region: region currently receiving the majority of traffic for the affected tenants.
- Target region(s): healthy region(s) selected to accept incrementally more traffic.
- Rehoming window: the period during which weights are adjusted and TTLs are managed. Typical window: 5–30 minutes depending on impact.
- Warm-seed: preloading KV/prefix caches and model KV caches in the target region with representative prefixes.

Pre-requisites (before initiating):
- Confirm cross-region capacity: target region GPU/CPU headroom >= projected new qps + 15% (check capacity dashboard).
- Confirm networking: egress/peering allocations for target regions are healthy and not rate-limited.
- Verify warm standby status for affected model versions in the target region (node count, quantization profile).
- Notify on-call SRE and downstream platform teams via incident channel.

Telemetry thresholds to watch (suggested):
- Region p95 latency (in ms): baseline and current. Trigger candidate if p95 > 2x baseline for 5m.
- 5m error rate (%): if error_rate > 1% absolute or > 3x baseline for 5m.
- Backend saturation: GPU utilization > 85% or CPU > 90% sustained for 3m.
- KV cache hit ratio: if hit_ratio drops > 10% after initial changes, pause and investigate.
- DNS 5xx from authoritative: any authoritative DNS errors are a hard-stop.

Decision matrix (operator heuristics):
- If latency high but errors low and backend not saturated: prefer traffic shaping + warm seeding to reduce tail latencies.
- If backend saturated AND KV hit ratio is still good: shift up to 25% traffic to targets in 5–10 minute increments.
- If backend saturated AND KV hit ratio already poor: consider smaller shifts (5–10%) with aggressive warm seeding.
- If authoritative DNS failing: abort progressive rehoming and escalate to SRE lead.

Step-by-step operator run (fast path):
1) Kickoff: create incident channel, annotate with current telemetry snapshot and chosen target region(s).
2) Warm seeding: run kv-seed job for top 1k prefixes: ops/kv-seed --region <target> --model <model-id> --prefix-list seeds/top-1k.txt & monitor job success.
3) Validate seeds: after seed job completes, validate target region kv_cache_hit_estimate > 30% for seeded prefixes.
4) Adjust routing weights: using routing console or CLI, set origin weight -> 90%, target weight -> 10% for first step. Command example: rtm set-weight --route global-api --region <origin> --weight 90 && rtm set-weight --route global-api --region <target> --weight 10
5) Observe for 5–7 minutes for latency, errors, and target saturation. If metrics stable, continue increments (90/10 -> 75/25 -> 50/50) spaced 7–10 minutes apart.
6) DNS TTL handling: keep authoritative TTLs unchanged during staged rehoming. For clients relying on short TTLs, do not lower TTLs — that causes cache churn. Use routing weight shifts rather than DNS TTL flips unless a full evacuation is required.
7) KV cache prefill for new prefixes: when traffic crosses a threshold to a target region (>25%), run background priming for the next 2k prefixes to avoid cold starts.
8) If errors spike or target saturation: rollback one step (e.g., 25% -> 10%), re-run warm seeding, and consider adding a secondary target region.
9) Once stable at final desired weights, update incident notes, and keep elevated monitoring for 1–2 hours before returning to normal operations.

Warm standby priming details:
- Seed lists: maintain per-customer prefix lists. For shared tenancy, seed top-global-prefixes for last 24h.
- Seeding rate: keep seeding throughput < 5% of target region ingress QPS to avoid priming-induced overload.
- KV seed TTLs: set seeded keys TTL to 15m for bootstrap; after stability, convert to standard TTLs.

DNS guidance and pitfalls:
- Avoid changing authoritative TTLs unless doing a full, irreversible failover. Lowering TTLs temporarily increases DNS queries and cache churn which harms warm caches.
- If performing DNS-based failover, coordinate with CDN and peering teams to avoid BGP flap-induced blackholes.

Rollback and abort criteria:
- Abort if authoritative DNS errors observed.
- Abort if target region GPU/CPU utilization > 95% or error rate > 2% absolute increase.
- Rollback one step if KV hit ratio drops > 15% compared to pre-shift baseline.

Post-incident checklist (quick):
- Collect and attach telemetry snapshots for origin & target for the rehoming window.
- Export KV seed job logs and success counts.
- Note decisions and timing for each weight change.
- File a follow-up ticket for capacity changes if target region was near max.

Drill plan (to validate this protocol):
- Quarterly tabletop: walk through 3 scenarios (partial backend overload, peering egress pressure, partial DNS authoritative slowdown).
- Live hack: in sandbox, simulate increased load in region A and run a progressive rehoming to region B. Measure cache hit ratio, P95 latency, and token costs.
- Success criteria: <10% request error rate delta, p95 increase < 50% vs baseline for seeded prefixes, KV hit ratio held within 10% of baseline.

Command snippets and dashboards to monitor quickly:
- Check region latency: obs query "latency.p95{region=<region>}"
- Check backend saturation: infra query "gpu.utilization{region=<region>}"
- Kick off kv seed: ops/kv-seed --region <region> --model <model> --prefix-list <file> --rate 100/s
- Adjust weights: rtm set-weight --route <route> --region <region> --weight <int>

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide authoritative guidance for multi-tenant customers with region affinity (sticky sessions). TODO: involve product networking for session affinity strategy.
- Automated warm-seeding: can we expose a single operator command that sequences seeding + weight updates? (Tracking: ENGSRE-7895)
- Metric to estimate "effective KV heat" for a region (composite score) — design proposal needed.

References and appendices:
- Related: progressive-egress-exercise-notes (confluence).
- Past incidents: incident-2025-03-multi-region-egress (see attached telemetry).

Notes to operator: keep communication tight. Progressive rehoming is delicate because it trades immediate client routing stability for preserved cache warmth. If in doubt, prefer smaller increments and more warm seeding rather than DNS TTL flips.

Document history:
- Drafted by Sofia Martinez (eng-sre) 2025-11-03
- Reviewed by Ethan Cole and Priya Nandakumar 2025-11-07
- Iteration: added seeding rate guidance 2025-11-10

End of draft.
